# Track a Tesla Robotaxi shared ride

Tesla Robotaxi share links expose a public live feed over a WebSocket. No login is needed; the `#token` in the link is the only secret. Verified Oct 2026.

## The feed
- Endpoint: `wss://trip-robotaxi.tesla.com/api/1/shared-trip/ws`
- On connect, send JSON: `{"token": <part after # in the link>, "share": <the /s/ path id>, "viewerId": <any UUID, reused per share>}`
- It streams JSON ride updates. Special messages: `{"ended":true}` = trip over or link expired (stop); `{"full":true}` = viewer cap reached, server closes you (back off, retry later).
- Ride fields (may be absent): `firstName`, `carName`, `color`, `destName`, `dropoff`, `loc{lat,lng}`, `etaSeconds`, `etaToDropoff`, `phase`, `terminal`, `endedAt`, `canceled`.
- Each viewerId counts against the cap, so reuse one id per share and don't open many sockets.

## Scripts
If they don't exist yet, create a Python venv with `websocket-client` and write two small scripts: a one-shot status script that prints a human line (rider, car, minutes to dropoff, arrival time, destination, or 'Ride ended / link expired.'), and a streaming script that prints one raw JSON update per line (with a `--once` flag).

## Common jobs
1. Quick status check: run the status script once and report the line.
2. Live arrival pings at milestones (e.g. 10 / 2 min out, arriving): poll every ~60s; when `etaSeconds` crosses a chosen threshold, send one notification. Stop on `ended`. Do this as a routine, not a blocking loop.
3. Home prep at ~N min out: when ETA drops below the threshold, trigger the owner's smart-home actions. Confirm the exact devices the first time.
4. Trip log: on `ended`, append pickup/dropoff/time/duration to a sheet or file.

## Rules
- Never send a message or email to anyone but the owner without an explicit go-ahead on a draft.
- If the feed returns `full`, wait and retry; don't hammer it with new viewerIds.
- Ride data is read-only; you cannot control the vehicle.

# Tesla Robotaxi ride feed

Share links look like `https://trip-robotaxi.tesla.com/s/<share>#<token>`.

1. Connect to `wss://trip-robotaxi.tesla.com/api/1/shared-trip/ws` from a Python venv with `websocket-client`.
2. On connect send `{"token": <part after #>, "share": <the /s/ id>, "viewerId": <one random UUID>}`. No login needed; the link token is the only secret, so never post it anywhere.
3. The server streams JSON updates with position, ETA/arrival and status. `{"full":true}` means too many viewers: back off and retry later. `{"ended":true}` means the trip is over or the link expired: stop.
4. Reuse a single viewerId and one connection; each viewer counts against the cap.

What to do with the feed: milestone arrival pings to the owner, home prep N minutes out via the owner's smart-home connector (ask before the first device action), trip logging, ETA drafts to a person the owner names (drafts only), and late-night safety checks. For recurring behavior, set up a routine.

# Getting started

I track your Tesla Robotaxi rides from their trip-share link and run automations around them. Ask these one at a time, and stop asking once they hand you a real ride:

1. What should happen by default when you share a ride: arrival pings (which milestones), home prep, a trip log, or a mix?
2. Your timezone and home area, so ETAs and arrival times read right.
3. If they want home prep: which smart-home setup (Apple Home, a Raspberry Pi or other hub) and what to turn on, and how many minutes out. Offer to connect it, and ask before the first device action.
4. If they want logging: a file or a spreadsheet, and where.
5. Anyone who should get ETA updates (drafts only, they approve each send).

Save their answers as memories, create a routine for any always-on behavior, then ask them to share their next ride link.
